paper.title_en: On the near-horizon interpretation of Krylov dynamics
paper.abstract_en: The Lanczos recursion maps operator growth onto the motion of a wave function on a semi-infinite chain, and for linearly growing Lanczos coefficients the deep region of the chain behaves like the near-horizon region of a black hole. We develop this correspondence in the time domain and determine how far it extends. Writing the Krylov equation as an exactly skew-adjoint difference operator, we derive a unitary continuum limit whose corrections are suppressed by $n^{-2}$ once the origin of the chain is fixed by the offset of the Lanczos coefficients. For $b_n\simeqαn$ the Krylov evolution is chiral transport in $\ln n$, which coincides with infalling waves near the horizon of an AdS$_2$ black hole when the Krylov depth is identified with the blueshift of an infalling particle; this fixes $α=πT$, while staggered configurations of the chain carry the outgoing chirality. For $b_n=α\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$ the correspondence is exact: the Krylov basis is the discrete series of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ carried by a bulk scalar of mass $m^2L^2=h(h-1)$, the Liouvillian is the boost generator of the black hole at temperature $T=α/π$, and positivity of $b_n^2$ reproduces the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound, saturated by strictly linear coefficients. Beyond leading order we prove that, for every Lanczos sequence with a smooth large-$n$ expansion, the ingoing solutions of the Krylov equation have coefficients polynomial in frequency to all orders in $1/n$, whereas a massive bulk field has a pole at the first special point $ω=-2πiT$ with residue proportional to $m^2$. Smooth subleading Lanczos data therefore cannot encode the bulk mass locally. The obstruction persists for the BTZ black hole, for which we obtain the Lanczos coefficients in closed form.
